assessments.support: Two named ABIDE-II sites, N by site/diagnosis given in Table 1, clear inclusion/exclusion criteria (neurological/psychiatric history, incomplete behavioral data, outlier/inconsistency scores).
Shen 268-node functional atlas, FC profiles with motion- and site-masked edges, clearly described preprocessing (FSL/AFNI steps listed).
BRIEF behavioral regulation subscale scores and SRS used as outcome; outlier/inconsistency exclusion criteria applied.

Leave-one-out and split-half cross-validation with permutation testing (5000 iterations) to assess significance properly; motion and site effects regressed from edges before modelling, reducing feature-selection leakage.

risk_of_bias.summary: Well-documented two-site ABIDE-II CPM study with quantitative motion threshold, named atlas, and leave-one-out plus permutation-based validation; a methodologically strong predictive-modelling example.

charting.title: Building functional connectivity neuromarkers of behavioral self-regulation across children with and without Autism Spectrum Disorder
charting.study_setting: Georgetown University (GU) and Kennedy Krieger Institute (KK) ABIDE-II sites
charting.comorbidities_included_excluded: Excluded: history of neurological or psychiatric disorders (psychiatric exclusion applied to TD group only), MRI contraindications, other medical problems preventing participation
charting.healthy_status_confirmed: TD group screened for absence of psychiatric disorder history
charting.dataset_openly_available: Uses public ABIDE-II GU and KK sites; CPM analysis code (MATLAB, BioImage Suite) is a general public toolbox (www.nitrc.org/projects/bioimagesuite), not a study-specific participant-list/code release
charting.specific_features: 268x268 Pearson correlation (Fisher z) functional connectivity matrix among Shen 268-node functional atlas ROIs, edges masked for motion/site association before modelling
charting.feature_extraction_tools: FSL and AFNI preprocessing (MCFLIRT motion correction, skull-stripping, 6mm FWHM smoothing); Shen 268-node atlas; Connectome Predictive Modelling (CPM, BioImage Suite, MATLAB)
charting.importance_method: CPM edge selection (positive/negative predictive edge networks)
charting.top_features_identified: Inhibition model: somato-motor, visual and cerebellar network edges; Shifting model: frontoparietal and dorsal attention network edges; both involved DMN and temporal-lobe edges
charting.model_category: Connectome-based predictive model (linear regression on selected FC edges)
charting.specific_algorithms: Connectome Predictive Modelling (CPM) with positive/negative edge selection
charting.validation_methodology: Leave-one-out cross-validation and split-half cross-validation, with permutation testing (5000 iterations) for significance
charting.performance_metrics: Spearman correlation (rs) between predicted and observed scores
charting.key_performance_results: Inhibition: rs=.23 (leave-one-out), permutation p=0.037; Shifting: rs=.19 (leave-one-out), permutation p=0.067 (not significant); Emotion control: rs<.05, not significant
charting.summary_key_findings: In 276 children (85 ASD, 191 TD) from two ABIDE-II sites, CPM models built on resting-state FC significantly predicted individual differences in inhibition and (at trend level) shifting behavioral-regulation scores via leave-one-out cross-validation, with distinct predictive brain networks for each subdomain, but did not significantly predict emotion control; ASD children scored significantly worse than TD on all three BRIEF subscales.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Both (group-difference + predictive/regression); ABIDE-II, GU and KK sites; n=276 (85 ASD / 191 TD), ages 8-13.
narrative_row.methods: FSL/AFNI preprocessing; Shen 268-node functional atlas; CPM with motion/site-masked edges; leave-one-out and split-half cross-validation with permutation testing for behavioral-regulation score prediction.
narrative_row.outcomes: ASD scored significantly worse than TD on all BRIEF subscales; FC-based CPM significantly predicted inhibition (rs=.23) and, at trend level, shifting (rs=.19), but not emotion control, with distinct predictive network topographies for each subdomain.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Shifting model did not survive permutation testing at the conventional threshold; no formal site harmonisation (ComBat) or leave-site-out evaluation; no study-specific code/participant list release beyond the general CPM toolbox.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A rigorous two-site ABIDE-II CPM example combining explicit motion thresholds, a named atlas, and leakage-aware leave-one-out/permutation validation — useful methodological benchmark for the knowledge graph.

kg_link.cohort_description: Two ABIDE-II sites (Georgetown University, Kennedy Krieger Institute); children aged 8-13 with BRIEF and resting-state fMRI; excluded for missing behavioral data, behavioral outliers/inconsistency, and >4mm maximum absolute head motion; final n=276 (85 ASD/191 TD).
kg_link.pipeline: FSL + AFNI (MCFLIRT motion correction, skull-stripping, 6mm FWHM smoothing)
kg_link.finding: Leave-one-out CPM significantly predicted inhibition (rs=.23, permutation p=0.037) and, at trend level, shifting (rs=.19, p=0.067) BRIEF behavioral-regulation scores from resting-state FC, with distinct predictive networks (posterior somato-motor/visual/cerebellar for inhibition, anterior frontoparietal/dorsal attention for shifting); emotion control was not predicted; ASD scored significantly worse than TD on all three BRIEF subscales.
